bugs: No correctness bugs found. Scalability nit: findCycleThrough walks the full transitive dependency closure of every added task, so building an n-task chain is O(n^2); flush() drains pendingEvents with shift(), which is O(n) per event.
strengths: Phase discriminated union makes illegal states unrepresentable and keeps attempt/timer handles attached to the state that owns them
Single attempt-identity check (isCurrent) covers late settles, timeouts and cancels uniformly
Binary heap with lazy invalidation via phase identity is simple and O(log n)
Timer creation deferred until after the start listener runs, so a start-listener cancel creates no timer
Outstanding test suite: timer accounting, global-timer/Date.now spies, unhandled-rejection traps, re-entrancy, __proto__ dep, mutation script
NOTES clearly separates PO-confirmed decisions from author decisions
weaknesses: Deferred event queue (pendingEvents/flushing flag) plus the pump loop with idleBefore is clever but non-obvious; almost no code comments to help a newcomer
Everything in one ~600-line file; heap sift logic duplicated inline rather than in a reusable module
Dependents tracked by id strings with repeated Map lookups and per-release every() scans
Tests reference external 'rule 12/13/14' numbering not present in the repo

bugs: No correctness bugs found. Minor: onIdle() called from a listener after the last task finished but before 'idle' is emitted resolves ahead of the idle event, unlike the documented ordering elsewhere; timeoutMs: Infinity is rejected (defensible, documented).
strengths: Clean module boundaries: reusable Heap and Emitter in src/internal
unmet counters plus dependents arrays plus forwardRefs make readiness O(1) per success and forward references explicit
Cycle search only runs when a forward reference to the new id exists, so normal add is O(deps)
All graph walks iterative and tested at 20k depth
Commit-then-emit discipline clearly stated and enforced; listeners always see final state
Good docstrings on every non-trivial method; unhandled-rejection guard in every test file; 300-task randomized ordering test
weaknesses: Three parallel structures (unmet, dependents, forwardRefs) must be kept consistent when extending
Emitter requires event names in both the type and a constructor list
NOTES defers the full decision record to an external spec.md that is not part of the deliverable
Test coverage of timer hygiene against real globals and of listener/cancel-from-start edge cases is thinner than X

bugs: findCycle in src/internal.ts is recursive and copies the path array at every level: adding a task to a deep dependency chain (~10k) overflows the call stack, and chain construction is O(depth^2) per add (cubic overall).
dispatch() does a linear scan of the queued Set for every start, making a large backlog O(n^2) to drain.
strengths: Single dependents index keyed by id (including unadded ids) handles forward refs, readiness and cascades uniformly
operate/dispatchAndCheckIdle re-entrancy model is easy to follow
onIdle() correctly waits for a pending idle transition instead of resolving ahead of it
Thorough NOTES enumerating open-behaviour decisions; helpful docstrings
Cascade is iterative with direct-dependency causes and add-order events
weaknesses: No priority queue; scalability of dispatch and cycle detection is poor
attemptFailed has subtle repeated state re-checks around abort that are easy to break
Tests: no unhandled-rejection guard, no real-timer/Date.now hygiene check, no start-listener-cancel or late-reject tests, cycle shape only asserted sorted
TimeoutError wrapper class adds surface without clear need

result.rationale: Y and X are both solid, bug-free implementations; Y edges ahead on design because its forward-ref/unmet-counter graph, targeted cycle check, extracted Heap/Emitter and iterative walks scale cleanly and are easy to extend, while X wins on testing with an exceptional behavioural suite covering timer hygiene, unhandled rejections and re-entrancy. X's deferred event queue and pump loop are correct but harder to onboard onto, and its per-add cycle walk is quadratic on chains. Z is readable and well documented but has real scalability defects: a recursive, path-copying cycle search that overflows on deep graphs and an O(n) linear scan per dispatch, plus a noticeably thinner test suite.
